key_insight: NH4SCN enables high-n quasi-2D perovskite scaffolds to template highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3, suggesting its benefit comes from improved 3D structure rather than transport through vertically oriented 2D layers.
engineering_relevance: Additive-controlled crystallisation offers a route to better-ordered solar-cell absorber films when quasi-2D and 3D phases have compatible lattices.
method: Probe NH4SCN-modified crystallisation using spectroscopy and structural analysis.
Identify suppression of n = 1 phases and promotion of high-n scaffolds through an extended nucleation window.
Assess lattice matching and cation-dependent templating of MAPbI3.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, but provides no numerical device-performance results.
watch_item: The mechanism is cation dependent and requires both close lattice matching and effective kinetic control, limiting direct transfer to other formulations.
paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
